input.quote: This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 imposes Singapore governing law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and effectively an exclusive foreign venue, which is walk-away territory. It also directly conflicts with Section 28.2, which gives exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County. The minimal fix aligns 28.1 with the preferred New York law/New York County venue pairing, leaving 28.2 and the pre-suit escalation in 28.3 intact.

proposal.summary: Replace Singapore law/venue in 28.1 with New York law, consistent with the New York County venue in 28.2
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction with New York law, which is our standard position and removes the conflict with the New York County venue already agreed in Section 28.2. Delaware, California, or England and Wales law with the courts of London would also work for us.

ops.oldText: This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
ops.newText: This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, and the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction.
